It claims cuts it didn't make, and its spin ('4.5-fold', addressing 'the three of you', 'regression to four') could backfire with hostile councillors. B's 'kids' line is a minor invention.

A delivers a clean, honest, ready-to-use rewrite that suits a hostile room, with the cost owned up front and trader spending data used early. B states a clearer spine and names the cost of removal, but it is buried in process clutter. It invents details, overstates figures ('nearly tripled', '4.5-fold') and contradicts its own cuts.

per_case.title: Museum visitor study told method by method
reasons: A gives a sharp spine and a timed, slide-by-slide outline that frames each method as triangulating evidence, which suits an academic audience. It does drop limitations and adds a few invented details. B is tighter but thinner, budgets only about 12 of 20 minutes, and misrepresents the studies as designed to answer the question.

B states a clear spine (the building hid the collection) and gives a slide-by-slide outline with usable opening lines, presenting the methods as triangulation. It is wordy, has timing inconsistencies, adds small invented details and drops limitations. A is concise, but it repeats the methods in a separate section after the results and is thinner overall.

per_case.title: Kelp talk buries its hopeful result
reasons: A gives a sharper spine: the fishers' sites as the mystery that breaks the pattern. Its opening hooks the room and reaches the twist within two minutes. B's order barely differs from the original, and it oddly downplays harvesting. Both invent small details. A adds some process clutter and drops harvesting from its opening.

B gives a sharper spine: fishers' practice explains the data. Its opening reaches the twist within two minutes, and it flags the need for a concrete practice. It has some clutter and invented details ("millions," "lab work"). A's opening never reaches the twist, and it oddly sidelines harvesting, which is central to why the co-managed sites worked.

per_case.title: Churn deck: price or support?
reasons: Both find the same onboarding/reseller spine. A misreads the data, claiming 55 of 61 new customers churned (90% cohort churn), and adds other unsupported claims that would embarrass the presenter. B reads the numbers correctly apart from a small ratio slip. It is tighter and rightly flags the one chart needed: MedPraxis versus direct churn rate.

Both reach the same root cause: reseller onboarding, with price and support as accelerants. B misreads the data, claiming '90% churn on this cohort' and conflating churned counts with cohort sizes, which would embarrass the presenter in front of leadership. B is also bloated. A is tighter and largely accurate, apart from a minor 2.7x slip, and flags the one missing chart.

per_case.title: Null SMS trial for ministry briefing
reasons: A gives a full scripted deck but contradicts the user's core constraint. It concludes 'voice calls work', recommends scaling, and misstates the design ('two arms'). It also adds invented details and process clutter. B is leaner and keeps voice explicitly exploratory. Its 'context, not memory' framing is honest, though its '12 slides' slip and thinner detail cost it.

A keeps the user's honesty constraint, treating the voice arm as a hypothesis worth properly testing, and offers a clear reframe. B's rebuilt deck is concrete, but it is padded with process clutter and oversells voice ('voice calls work', 'scale voice'). It also invents subgroup numbers and misstates the design as two arms, which is exactly the spin the user wanted to avoid.

per_case.title: Reorg memo hides the actual change
reasons: B gives a clean, voice-faithful rewrite with a scannable announcement. It keeps the ledger thanks and gives a brief answer on the stat. A's 'structure not people' line is good, but A is padded with process jargon and says 'Monday' for a 1 November change. It also invents 'every conversation' and adds salesy overpromises. B's 'four separate teams' phrasing is a minor flaw.

B's rewrite has a stronger spine. 'This is a structure problem, not a people problem' resolves the blame worry directly, and the reorg reads as the fix. A is tighter but still says teams are 'blocked waiting on Platform' and misstates that Platform 'becomes four teams.' B is padded with process jargon and invents 'every conversation' with leads.

per_case.title: Outage postmortem is just a timeline
reasons: A rebuilds the timeline into a causal failure chain and a ready-to-present postmortem with owned, prioritised actions, which is what the manager asked for. But it invents facts: a 19:30 sale start, no circuit breaker, and a 5xx cascade. It is also padded. B is faithful and concise but stops at advice.

B delivers a near-ready postmortem built around a clear causal-chain spine, with prioritised actions and no-blame framing. That is what's needed for Wednesday. It does invent details (19:30 sale start, missing circuit breaker, '5-minute fix') and miscounts time, so it needs editing. A is accurate and tight but only advises; it doesn't rebuild the document.

per_case.title: Nurse burnout: staffing or scheduling story?
reasons: Both reach the same sequenced story. A buries it in process clutter: rotations, self-scores and piece lists. It also invents costs, IT readiness and dates, and overclaims that nurses aren't citing busyness, which is the cherry-picking the user feared. B honestly says scheduling didn't create the vacancies. It is concise and usable, though it misstates 'tripled'.

Both reach the same sequencing idea: fix ShiftGrid now and use the results for the April staffing case. A stays honest about confounds but miscalls 3.1→5.8 'tripled' and invents a 5–10 point estimate. B buries its script in process clutter, invents costs and IT readiness, and overclaims ('alone explains most'), risking the cherry-picking the user feared.

per_case.title: Roadmap decision doc feels off
reasons: A finds the stronger spine: B is a prerequisite for A, not a rival. It also supplies recommendation text ready for the doc. It loses points for process clutter, a muddled farmer-upload mechanism, and a timeline that pilots the 8-week dashboard in week 7. B is more accurate and asks the key question, whether processors will wait, but its conditional recommendation is muddled.

Both spot that bad collection data undermines the forecast dashboard. A stays accurate: the 9% error applies to the 40% paper centres. It also names the real unknown, whether processors will wait. B's rebuilt recommendation has an impossible timeline, piloting A in week 7 despite an 8-week build. It overstates the data error, invents a causal chain and adds diagram and meta clutter.

per_case.title: Charity board paper rests on one interview
reasons: A gives a clear diagnosis, that the role became unmanageable and pay is not the sole cause, plus a rebuilt outline. However, it is padded and misstates facts, turning two 'final straw' remarks into three and asserting why staff left. B is accurate and tight, with pragmatic advice, but offers no rebuilt structure.

A pinpoints the central gap: many causes named, only pay addressed. It gives tight, actionable fixes without distorting the evidence. B offers a fuller rebuilt outline, but it is bloated with process clutter. Its draft also misstates facts ('three' said final straw, 'they did not leave for money'), errors an ex-HR trustee would catch.

per_case.title: Shared lab equipment memo for Dean
reasons: Both answers reframe the issue as a structural cost-model failure with a clear ask. A gives a fuller draft, but it is buried in process clutter and invents facts: 'meant to be temporary', 'two years later', Chemistry's details. It also drops the $68k figure. B is tighter, faithful to the notes and ready to build on, though it stops short of full prose.

B delivers a usable one-page memo with a clear spine, an explicit ask tied to the February renewal, and a structural-not-managerial framing. It is padded with process clutter and invents details such as the 'temporary' arrangement and Chemistry's billing. A is tighter but gives only an outline, and it reverses who subsidises whom.

per_case.title: Loyalty app flop review, need it tomorrow
reasons: A has the sharper spine, but it adds process clutter and overclaims: it invents a 'kill the app' ultimatum and says firmware 'explains the whole miss' when even new-firmware stores reach only 11.8%. B is a tight, ready-to-speak script with ranked, concrete asks. Its flaws are minor: a store-count slip (11 instead of 16) and a 'three vs two' inconsistency.

A gives a tight, ready-to-speak 5-minute script with a clear ask: accelerate firmware, retrain, relaunch. B has a sharper spine but adds an invented 'kill the app' ultimatum and an '80%' figure. It claims firmware 'explains the whole miss' despite 11.8% vs 25%, and buries the script in process clutter, which is bad for a rushed user.

per_case.title: Studio delay note: apology vs defence
reasons: A delivers a usable rebuilt note in which the summer work is honoured without defending the crunch, which directly answers the cut-or-keep question. However, it is padded with ASCII diagrams, and it adds details Bartek never wrote, such as the unbudgeted rebuild and 'call me on it'. B's diagnosis is sound, but it offers only a rough outline and ends with a question.

B finds a sharper spine (ownership, cost, structural change) and delivers a rebuilt, ready-to-send note. It does overreach: it drops the budget line, hardens 'likely', and adds an invented 'hadn't budgeted' detail, and the diagrams are clutter. A diagnoses reasonably but offers only a rough outline and ends with a question.

per_case.title: Document system paper reads like vendor comparison
reasons: Both reframe the paper around the cost of fragmentation. A writes a fuller draft but invents details: Option B/C costs, a phased timeline and a claimed 6-week break-even from full recapture. A cost-sensitive committee would challenge these. B gives a cleaner, credible structure with ROI framing and moves the feature table to an appendix, despite a minor arithmetic slip.

A finds the same problem-first spine and gives a clean six-part structure in a fraction of the length. Its '3x' payback is a slip: a 5% gain roughly equals the 465k cost. B is bloated with diagrams and process commentary. It invents an Option B cost, features and implementation phases, and claims the full SGD 9–10M is saved, which a cost-sensitive committee would challenge.

per_case.title: Permit backlog report contradicts its recommendation
reasons: A finds the real spine: rework multiplies workload, so headcount becomes a stabilizer while intake is fixed. It delivers a rebuilt section and a script for the boss. It is bloated with rotations and invents costs, FTE splits and timelines. B is concise and politically sound but offers no rebuilt draft and misreads the 61% figure.

A spots the gap between the 61% rework finding and the headcount ask, and gives a usable script for the boss. B's rebuilt draft has a clearer spine, but it buries it in rotation clutter. It also invents costs, FTE splits, timelines and shaky workload math, then claims it only rearranged facts. Council would tear those numbers apart.
